approach: Root cause: a plan demonstration (DemonstrationOutput, stored as Demonstration) has method, command, observes and fails_without, and no field for the test seam. Nothing makes the planner name the entry point, the fake or fixture and its injection, or whether the seam exists. Athena's own plan check, `admission::plan_findings`, therefore cannot require it, and the critic sees nothing to confirm, so nonexistent seams surfaced only in round 3 (jobs 20261018-095726-r3bn, 20261018-113512-gvcs, 20261024-115052-bzw6). Fix: add a `seam` field to the planner's output schema (its doc comment is the instruction the planner reads) and to the stored record (optional, serde default, skipped when none, so old records parse and re-serialize byte-identically). `plan_findings` gets a Major finding for a behavior criterion whose demonstration has an empty or missing seam, next to the existing fails_without check. It names the criterion and sends the plan back mechanically with no critic call. `demonstration_lines` in briefs.rs renders "Test seam:" under each demonstration, so the critic and verifier read it. The critic checks that the seam exists in the code; Athena does not. Existing test fixtures that give a behavior criterion a fails_without must also give a seam. Add unit and end-to-end tests, a record round-trip test and a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Put the refusal in `admission::plan_findings`, beside the fails_without check, as a Major finding. It is not a new function in planning.rs. planning.rs gets the field copied through `plan_record` and the new gate takes effect there via the existing `plan_findings` call.
decisions.reason: plan_findings is the one place for Athena's plan rules (its doc lists them). It already runs after the planner output parses and before the critic. A Major finding there reuses the mechanical-revision loop (2 passes, no critic call, finding text shown to the planner). The planner's next prompt then carries the fix. This is the origin of the gap: the rule list lacked the seam rule.

rejected.option: A separate seam check in planning.rs after plan_record
rejected.why: Splits Athena's plan rules across two files; the next rule would again be added in the wrong place.

rejected.option: Only describe the seam in the planner prompt
rejected.why: Prose-only; the failure repeated five times with prompt text. The user default 'mechanism' requires enforcement by code.

rejected.option: Make `seam` a required, non-optional String on every demonstration
rejected.why: Content criteria have no seam to name, and old stored plans would not parse.

decisions.choice: `seam: Option<String>` in DemonstrationOutput (no serde default, like fails_without, so the schema lists the key) and `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] Option<String>` in the record.
decisions.reason: Mirrors fails_without, which is required only for behavior criteria. Option keeps content criteria and old records valid. In the record, skip-if-none keeps old plan records round-tripping unchanged (the same approach as `resumed_from`). Serde treats a missing Option key as None, so the existing fixtures that omit `seam` still parse.

rejected.option: A structured seam (entry_point, fake, status) with three fields
rejected.why: More schema and record surface for the same information. A single text field with a doc comment naming the three parts is the smallest design, and the critic reads text anyway.

decisions.choice: Athena checks only that the seam is present and non-blank for a behavior criterion. The critic checks that it exists in the code.
decisions.reason: Matches the out-of-scope line 'Mechanically proving a seam exists'. The brief already gives the critic Read, Grep and Glob.

rejected.option: Parse the seam for 'exists' or 'added by step'
rejected.why: Brittle free-text parsing that rejects good plans; out of scope.

decisions.choice: Render the seam in the shared `demonstration_lines` as an indented line `  Test seam: ...` after the Run line.
decisions.reason: One function renders demonstrations for the critic brief, the producer plan section and the verifier brief. All three readers see the seam, and the producer-section hash is computed from the same text.

rejected.option: Render only in the critic brief
rejected.why: The producer and verifier would not see the seam they must build or exercise.

decisions.choice: Touch `crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs`, `crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs` and the three athena-cli test fixtures (job_plan.rs, lifecycle.rs, introspection.rs), though they are not in the expected deliverables. Do not touch run/mod.rs or status.rs unless the compiler requires it.
decisions.reason: The gate cannot live elsewhere without splitting the rules. Without the fixture and fake-planner updates, the new rule would refuse their behavior-criterion plans (the default reading's criterion 2 is behavior) and break cargo test. The expected deliverables run/mod.rs and status.rs construct no Demonstration literal I could find (status.rs:2350 has `demonstrations: vec![]`; mod.rs only imports the type), so I expect no edit there.

rejected.option: Skip the seam rule when the plan comes from the fake planner
rejected.why: Special-cases the gate and hides the field from end-to-end tests.

risks.risk: Existing planned-job tests (athena-cli job_plan.rs, lifecycle.rs, introspection.rs, and the fake planner) give a behavior criterion a demonstration with no seam and would be refused.
risks.mitigation: Update each fixture and the fake planner to supply a seam in the same change. Run the full `cargo test --locked`. job_plan.rs's existing `athena_checks_a_demonstration_for_every_criterion_and_a_fails_without...` test keeps its expectations.

risks.risk: Real planners will have more rounds refused because they omit the seam. This is intended (criterion 6). A planner that always omits it burns the 2 mechanical passes and stops the job.
risks.mitigation: The finding text says exactly what to add, the schema doc comment names the three parts, and the mechanical loop does not use up a critic round. The planner brief has token room, but no prompt edit is planned; it can be added if the refusal rate proves high.

risks.risk: The seam is free text, so a planner can write a hollow seam (for example 'exists') and pass the Athena check.
risks.mitigation: This is accepted and out of scope. The critic is shown the seam in the brief and can check it with Read/Grep/Glob. A later change can add critic frame text if hollow seams appear.

risks.risk: Adding a field to a stored record type could break old records or the byte-identical round trip.
risks.mitigation: Serde default plus skip_serializing_if on the record; a test parses an old record without the key and asserts the re-serialized text equals the original.

risks.risk: The end-to-end test rewrites the reader output to a behavior criterion, and the behavior reading might fail acceptance or verification checks in the fake harness.
risks.mitigation: Assert on planning-stage behavior only (planner and critic calls, prompts, stop reason). The unit test in admission.rs carries the core assertion without the harness.

risks.risk: Token budgets: the schema doc comment is part of the planner's output schema, not an always-loaded prompt set, but a `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` test exists.
risks.mitigation: No prompt or system-facts file changes. Run `cargo test` to confirm the budget tests still pass.

demonstrations.method: Two tests in athena-core. (a) Unit test in admission.rs tests: build a JobPlan literal (the `findings_for_path` helper there shows how) and a `reading()` with one Behavior criterion. Call `plan_findings` with a verifier Policy whose command list allows `cargo test`. (b) End-to-end test in run/tests.rs using `repo_with_planning`, `run_planned` and `planning_script` (all exist today). The reader output is rewritten so criterion 1 is `behavior` and the plan has a `cargo test` demonstration with a fails_without; the producer and verifier stay on the base fake script.
demonstrations.observes: Unit test: a behavior demonstration with seam None, `""` or `"   "` gives a Major Athena finding at location `demonstrations, criterion 1` whose summary names 'criterion 1' and 'seam'. The same plan with a seam gives no seam finding. A content criterion with no seam gives none. End-to-end test: a planner queue of [plan without seam, plan with seam] shows the second planner prompt containing the seam finding and no critic call before it; a queue of only the seamless plan stops with a reason containing 'after 2 mechanical revisions' and the criterion, and never calls the critic, producer or verifier. The end-to-end test asserts planner and critic roles and prompts, not Landed (a behavior reading may not verify with the fake verifier).
demonstrations.fails_without: Before the change `plan_findings` has no seam rule. The seamless plan yields no Major seam finding, so the unit assertions fail; in the end-to-end test the critic is called on round 1 (the critic queue is empty or the roles differ) and the stop reason is missing. The `seam` field also does not exist, so the with-seam plan does not compile or parse.
